commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Use tensor_ext bitcast for sub-byte packing

- Bitcast packed weights with iree_tensor_ext.bitcast instead of
  flow.tensor.bitcast, the op for bitcasts created before dispatch
  formation. The compiled modules are byte-identical.
- Document in the PropagateAffineQuantization description that pads are
  not moved onto sub-byte storage.
- Correct the comments on the hoisting size limit.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing the layouts during global optimization makes that phase
target aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding
tensor graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their
epilogues and result unpacks.

Add the experimental --iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling flag. It
takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags, so
conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the
route uses the operation families and encoding strategy of
dispatch-time data tiling.

The route applies to modules with a single llvm-cpu target on x86_64 or
AArch64 that uses the CPU encoding resolver without inner-tiled layouts,
and only with the default encoding strategy. For these modules, global
optimization propagates reshapes, normalizes contraction dimensions,
assigns and propagates encodings, and materializes them on the host. It
then records the target on the module, even if nothing was data-tiled.
Dispatch creation therefore skips encoding assignment for the whole
module, always fuses data-tiled ops with their epilogues and result
unpacks, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions. Other
modules keep dispatch-time data tiling. The enable_inner_tiled check
moves from the CPU encoding models to the Codegen utilities, so that the
eligibility check can share it.

On an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32, median of 10), the route is within
noise of dispatch-time data tiling for a matmul with bias and ReLU, a
batch matmul with ReLU and a convolution with ReLU. x86_64 has not been
measured.

The optimization options reference documents the route, its limits and
the flag precedence.

The layout decision is split over several passes, supports one CPU
target per module, and adds HAL and Codegen dependencies to the global
phases. The TODOs describe moving it into its own component that decides
per affinity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Fold batch_matmul broadcasts through affine dequantization

Shared quantized weights reach a batch_matmul in two forms: dequantized
at their native rank and then broadcast, or broadcast as integers and
then dequantized. FoldBroadcastIntoBatchMatmul already folds the first
form. The second left a batch-sized dequantize feeding a full-rank
batch_matmul: with QDQ conversion the integer contraction read a
materialized integer broadcast, and without it the weights were
dequantized once per batch element.

Extend the fold's producer matcher to recognize a dequantize whose value
input is a broadcast (a linalg.broadcast or a broadcasting, possibly
permuting, generic). In one step, the rewrite builds a dequantize of the
broadcast's source at the source's rank and composes the broadcast map,
through the dequantize's value maps, into the contraction operand map,
using the same named-or-generic decision as the direct fold. No broadcast
is ever placed between the dequantize and the contraction, so both forms
reach the same canonical form before QDQ conversion.

The rewrite fires only when:
- the dequantize result has the contraction as its only user, so the
  dequantize shrinks instead of being duplicated; the broadcast may have
  other users, which keep it;
- no scale or zero-point map depends on a dimension the broadcast
  introduces, since such parameters vary across the broadcast.
Scale and zero-point maps are rebased onto the source's dims; operands
and attributes (signedness, clamp bounds, zero-point presence) are
carried over verbatim. Dynamic dims are taken from the source.

Tests: pass-level cases for per-channel, asymmetric, per-tensor unsigned,
transposed input and output maps, dynamic batch, M and weight dims, LHS,
generic broadcasts, a multi-use broadcast, and the non-firing multi-use
dequantize and batch-varying scale and zero point. New stage-boundary
tests run Form A, Form B, asymmetric Form B, transposed weights in both
forms and a dynamic batch through the global optimization pipeline with
QDQ conversion off and on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

form. The second left a batch-sized dequantize feeding a full-rank
batch_matmul: with QDQ conversion the integer contraction read a
materialized integer broadcast, and without it the weights were
dequantized once per batch element.

Extend the fold's producer matcher to recognize a dequantize whose value
input is a broadcast (a linalg.broadcast or a broadcasting, possibly
permuting, generic). In one step, the rewrite builds a dequantize of the
broadcast's source at the source's rank and composes the broadcast map,
through the dequantize's value maps, into the contraction operand map,
using the same named-or-generic decision as the direct fold. No broadcast
is ever placed between the dequantize and the contraction, so both forms
reach the same canonical form before QDQ conversion.

The rewrite fires only when:
- the dequantize result has the contraction as its only user, so the
  dequantize shrinks instead of being duplicated; the broadcast may have
  other users, which keep it;
- no scale or zero-point map depends on a dimension the broadcast
  introduces, since such parameters vary across the broadcast.
Scale and zero-point maps are rebased onto the source's dims; operands
and attributes (signedness, clamp bounds, zero-point presence) are
carried over verbatim. Dynamic dims are taken from the source.

Tests: pass-level cases for per-channel, asymmetric, per-tensor unsigned,
transposed input and output maps, dynamic batch, M and weight dims, LHS,
generic broadcasts, a multi-use broadcast, and the non-firing multi-use
dequantize and batch-varying scale and zero point. New stage-boundary
tests run Form A, Form B, asymmetric Form B, transposed weights in both
forms and a dynamic batch through the global optimization pipeline with
QDQ conversion off and on.

  formation. The compiled modules are byte-identical.
- Document in the PropagateAffineQuantization description that pads are
  not moved onto sub-byte storage.
- Correct the comments on the hoisting size limit.

[GlobalOptimization] Use tensor_ext bitcast for sub-byte packing

- Bitcast packed weights with iree_tensor_ext.bitcast instead of
  flow.tensor.bitcast, the op for bitcasts created before dispatch
  formation. The compiled modules are byte-identical.
- Document in the PropagateAffineQuantization description that pads are
  not moved onto sub-byte storage.
- Correct the comments on the hoisting size limit.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Use tensor_ext bitcast for sub-byte packing

- Bitcast packed weights with iree_tensor_ext.bitcast instead of
  flow.tensor.bitcast, the op for bitcasts created before dispatch
  formation. The compiled modules are byte-identical.
- Document in the PropagateAffineQuantization description that pads are
  not moved onto sub-byte storage.
- Correct the comments on the hoisting size limit.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[CMake] Honor LLVM tool overrides in the compiler with installed SDKs (#25167)

The installed-LLVM configuration currently overwrites explicitly
supplied tool and Clang resource-header paths.

Hence if i fetch llvm/mlir libraries from a channel like conda-forge or
so I won't be able to use them.

We should preserve those overrides so package-manager installations can
supply native tools separately, while keeping the existing defaults when
no override is provided.

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Share the im2col gather with the QDQ input window sum

A quantized convolution with a weight zero point needs the sum of every
input window, which ConvertQDQToIntegerMath emits as a conv-shaped
reduction over the original input. With the QDQ rewrite now running
before im2col, that reduction gathered every window a second time in
its own dispatch, which cost about as much as the im2col itself and
made asymmetric convolutions slower than the float path.

Give the window sum's shape-only operand the partner operand's map
restricted to the sum's loops, so the sum reads like a convolution with
a ones filter and convolution dimension inference recognizes it. Then
let ConvertConvToIm2Col rewrite a convolution without output channel
reuse when its gather is identical to the gather of another rewritten
convolution: the pass collects those gather keys (input value, read
map, static sizes) before applying patterns, and CSE merges the two
gathers. The window sum becomes a row reduction over the shared
im2col result. Unshared pooling and depthwise convolutions, dynamic
gather shapes, and plain matmul sums are unchanged.

Apple M4, llvm-cpu, data tiling and ukernels, one worker, asymmetric
NCHW 3x3 with C_in 16, 28x28, C_out 32: 0.138 ms before, 0.065 ms
after, against 0.116 ms for the float path. 5x5 and 7x7 improve
similarly; symmetric and matmul cases are unchanged. The gather merges
for NCHW and NHWC with stride 2, dilation 2 and batch 2, and the
output is bit-identical to the float path on the tested inputs.

[GlobalOpt] Share the im2col gather with the QDQ input window sum

A quantized convolution with a weight zero point needs the sum of every
input window, which ConvertQDQToIntegerMath emits as a conv-shaped
reduction over the original input. With the QDQ rewrite now running
before im2col, that reduction gathered every window a second time in
its own dispatch, which cost about as much as the im2col itself and
made asymmetric convolutions slower than the float path.
